newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent trades up, some traders see swaps play.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent trades up, some traders see swaps play.

text.p: Two Dated Brent crude cargoes traded firmer on Thursday, dividing traders into those who say it reflected the market and those who suspected the buyer sought higher numbers to benefit a derivatives position.

"It can't be worth that much," a trader said of the March 14-16 loaders traded at April Brent +55 cents. This is sharply up from a March 6-8 loader traded at April +48 on Tuesday and a March 13-15 done at March Brent +5 cents on Wednesday.
"They are clearly trying to keep the quotes up," another said of the buyer, was described this week as seeking to inflate the Brent benchmark to boost profits from a swaps position.

The buyer has declined to comment on allegations that he seeks to benefit from swaps plays. On Thursday the buyer also declined to comment on continuing talk that he was sending two VLCCs of Brent to South Africa.
CFD values pointed to slightly higher values. March 3-7 traded at April +23 and +27 cents, compared to closing quotes of +22/+25 on Wednesday.
The following week was talked at April +6/+10 cents, two cents firmer. March 17-21 was steady at April -20/-17.
On paper March/April was steady at Dated +42/45 cents, while April/May was unchanged at +31/34.
May/June was around four cents easier at +17/20.
April Brent traded unchanged at $19.70 after business on Wednesday at $19.71 and $19.55.
Other North Sea grades were tight but discussions were muted after Wednesday's busy action.
"First half March is pretty well all mopped up. The exception is Ekofisk because of loading problems and the differential looks unhappy," a trader said.
